findings.quote: **Stop and answer.** A static route and a propagated route both name 172.16.0.0/16. Which one wins? ... The static route, for [the same destination CIDR block]
findings.evidence: The answer contradicts the table directly above it, where row 1 'BGP propagated routes from an Direct Connect connection' beats row 2 'Manually added static routes' (site-to-site-vpn-route-priority-dx-bgp-before-vpn-static-before-vpn-bgp, scope: virtual private gateway route selection). The linked fact site-to-site-vpn-static-route-beats-propagated-same-cidr has scope 'VPC route table' and only covers 'static routes whose targets are an internet gateway, a virtual private gateway, a network interface, an instance ID, a VPC peering connection, a NAT gateway, a transit gateway, or a gateway VPC endpoint' (docs/vpn/latest/s2svpn/vpn-route-priority). The text never says there are two levels (the VPC route table, then the virtual private gateway's own choice among VPN and Direct Connect routes), so the reader learns 'static always wins' and 'Direct Connect BGP beats static' at the same time. Fix: name the layer in the prompt (a static route in the VPC route table versus a route that the virtual private gateway propagates) and add one cause-and-effect sentence that separates the two levels.
findings.resolution: fix-12: see claims-12-02. The prompt names the subnet route table, and the answer separates the two levels.

findings.quote: | Not on | [Dedicated or hosted connection of any speed](../facts/direct-connect.md#direct-connect-vif-transit-access-transit-gateways-any-speed) | [Not supported on 1 Gbps dedicated connections] ... |

findings.quote: **Stop and answer.** A private virtual interface on a virtual private gateway in us-east-1 must reach a VPC in eu-west-1. What do you add? ... A Direct Connect gateway.

findings.quote: **Stop and answer.** MACsec negotiation fails in the default mode. Does traffic stop? ... No. It can [fall back to unencrypted communication].
